newsitem.title: portugal: RALLYING-ERIKSSON HOLDS SLIM LEAD IN PORTUGAL.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-ERIKSSON HOLDS SLIM LEAD IN PORTUGAL.

text.p: Sweden's Kenneth Eriksson held a slender lead in the Rally of Portugal on Tuesday as nearest rival and world champion Tommi Makinen of Finland closed to within one second after 17 stages.

Eriksson, driving a Subaru, had started the second leg of the rally, the fourth on this year's calendar, with a 14-second lead over Makinen's Mitsubishi, but slowly lost his advantage on the four morning stages.
"Eriksson has had no problems at all, but Makinen is pushing very hard," said a spokesperson for the Subaru team.
"The stages are still very dusty which is making conditions quite difficult, but he is feeling quite confident."

Belgian Freddy Loix maintained his third position in the Toyota, more than one minute behind the leading two cars, while Portuguese Rui Madeira moved up to fourth place in his Subaru following the retirement of Briton Richard Burns in the Mitsubishi.

Burns, who finished second in the Safari Rally three weeks ago, had looked set for another points-scoring finish when he had suspected engine problems on the road sections between the 16th and 17th stages.
Tuesday's remaining five stages will take the teams to an overnight halt at Viseu, before the final leg on Wednesday sees them return to the coastal base of Figueira da Foz.
